item.title: Valentine's Day spending expected to reach a record high
item.description: The National Retail Federation is projecting that $29.1 billion will be spent by consumers for Valentine's Day, with candy, flowers, cards and jewelry being the top gifts.

item.title: Elevators fixed at Jenny Lind apartments, but residents say more problems remain
item.description: After years of complaints, the elevators at the Jenny Lind Apartments have finally been repaired, providing relief to residents who had to struggle to climb multiple flights of stairs.

item.title: Chiefs, Branson vacation destination agreement comes to an end
item.description: The City of Branson, Missouri announced Friday that its contract with the Kansas City Chiefs is coming to an end on May 15, 2026.

item.title: Five people indicted for alleged $220M cattle fraud scheme, fugitive from Strafford
item.description: Five people, including two from Missouri, have been indicted for an alleged cattle fraud scheme, in which they falsely represented to individual cattle purchasers that Agridime would use their funds to purchase specific individual cattle for each victim, raise the cattle, and eventually sell the meat from the same specific individual cattle for a profit.

item.title: Northern Greene County neighbors push back on proposed battery storage site
item.description: Neighbors in Greene County, Missouri are opposing a proposed Battery Energy Storage System facility due to concerns about fire risk, noise, light pollution, and the difficulty of extinguishing lithium battery fires.
